messages:
sasha: Quick sync — thinking through an "audit-merge" approach for metering. TL;DR: we currently produce raw token events and a separate finalization pass that emits billing events. I want to converge them so the canonical stream is 'billing-ready' but still retain replayable provenance. Tradeoffs?

matt: ugh saga. do you mean collapsing raw->billing inline during ingest?

sasha: not inline for every request. proposal is a two-stage model: ingest raw events -> lightweight enrichment -> emit provisional billing events into a partitioned topic -> a periodic compaction/merge job that canonicalizes and seals final billing rows with provenance pointers.

nina: benefit is downstream consumers only need one topic for billing. downside: harder to inspect intermediate raw events for audits. how do we keep provenance?

sasha: keep an immutable provenance envelope per billing row pointing to the raw event ids + transform version. e.g. billing_row.provenance = [raw_event_id1, raw_event_id2] and a transform_hash. we store provenance in cold storage + index small pointer in row.

devon: that sounds reasonable. how do we handle late arrivals and corrections? watermarking + tombstones?

sasha: idea: each partition has a windowed finalize watermark. before watermark you can issue provisional billing (version N). after watermark, compactor seals final version (N+sealed) and emits a tombstone for older provisional rows. corrections produce a new sealed row with a higher version.

matt: we need idempotency keys for transforms. otherwise replays will duplicate tokens. Suggest a deterministic signature per logical request: sha256(customer_id + request_ts + model_hash + token_count + prompt_hash).

sasha: agreed. plan to add `transform_sig` and `source_tuple` to raw events. compactor uses transform_sig as merge key.

alyssa: storage/cost question — storing full provenance arrays for every row could be big. pointers only, right? small vector of ids or a checkpoint blob index.
sasha: yes pointers only in the hot row. full provenance blob in long-term object store keyed by provenance_id. compactor writes blobs atomically.

nina: audit tooling: how do auditors replay end-to-end? they need to reconstruct final tokens and prompts. can we embed a small sample of the canonicalized prompt and hashed tokens in the sealed row to speed queries?
sasha: add `sample_digest` field (sha256 of first 1k chars + token histogram) — gives quick diff checks. full replay still pulls provenance blob and raw events.

matt: what about duplicate detection across ingestion shards? we've seen races when client retries land on different shards. transform_sig helps but we also need a global idempotency index. maybe a TTL'd cache (redis/mem) + compactor dedupe on transform_sig at merge time.
sasha: compactor is the final dedupe authority; we can also have a nearline cache to reduce noise. compactor will keep the highest-priority event (tie-breaker: earliest arrival_ts or lowest event_id depending on policy).

devon: policy question: which wins when revisions arrive after seal? customer dispute vs system correction. we need a clear semantics: sealed rows are append-only; revisions create a new sealed revision. billing system consumes latest sealed revision per key. ledger picks up delta.

sasha: yes sealed rows are immutable; we keep revisions as new sealed rows with revision_number++. downstream reconcile uses (customer_id, billing_key, latest_revision).

alyssa: ops concerns: compactor load spikes. compaction should be incremental and region-aware. We must avoid global compaction windows.
sasha: agreed. do per-account / per-shard compaction windows + async merge queues. also rate-limit finalization to keep latency predictable.

nina: quick proto for compactor merge SQL pattern?
sasha: example: ```sql
-- merge provisional into sealed
MERGE INTO billing_sealed t
USING provisional p
ON t.transform_sig = p.transform_sig
WHEN MATCHED AND p.version > t.version THEN
  UPDATE SET amount = p.amount, provenance_id = p.provenance_id, version = p.version
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN
  INSERT (transform_sig, customer_id, amount, provenance_id, version)
;```

matt: nice. include a cheksum column for row-level integrity.

sasha: will add `row_checksum` and `provenance_id` write-after-commit. compactor writes provisional -> upload provenance blob -> compute blob_id -> commit sealed row with blob_id. atomicity via two-phase commit style but implemented with idempotent operations and compare-and-swap on metadata store.

devon: monitoring/alerts: need to track compaction lag, number of pending provisional rows, blob upload failures, and sealing error rate. set SLOs for compaction latency per tier (hosted/dedicated/private).

sasha: noted. I'll draft an RFC with sequence diagram + cost estimate. action items: @matt add transform_sig generation in ingest lib; @alyssa sketch compactor autoscaling knobs; @nina audit UX — a query path to reconstruct replay; @devon define policies for dispute vs correction. I'll ping earlier when RFC is up. :thumbsup:

ingest-bot: Replay job started for partition p-17 at offset 124512 (requested by sasha).

sasha: thanks. small follow-up — we should include a human-readable `transform_version` string in rows so we can quickly see which codepath created a row (e.g. v1.3-compact-2026-03).

alyssa: agreed. helps debugging.

matt: one last note: embeddings/embedding-attribution will need a similar pattern but different dedupe key (embedding hash). keep design generic.

sasha: yep. RFC will call out extension points for other signal types. ending thread here, will open RFC doc.
